items.message: The `label` parameter is passed directly to `gh issue list --label <label>` via `subprocess.run`. If `label` arrives from an untrusted caller (e.g., the workflow arg `label: str = "wayfinder"` in `lockstep.py`), a value like `wayfinder --jq .[] --exec some_command` could inject additional `gh` flags or abuse gh's own flag parsing. Issue body text returned by `gh issue list` is placed directly into `Ticket.description` and then parsed by `blockers_in()` for `Blocked by:` lines. Anyone who can write a GitHub issue body (i.e., any repo collaborator, or an attacker who has filed an issue) controls which ticket keys appear in `blocked_by`, and therefore which tickets the adapter considers blocked or on the frontier. `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))` prepends the example directory — a user-controlled location — to the module search path. Any `.py` file named `wayfinder`, `in_lockstep`, `github_map`, or any other name imported later that is placed in that directory will shadow the intended module.
